question: Two rounds into designing a Claude-assisted induction pack, an education team finds the drafts are accurate but pitched at the wrong level for new teaching assistants. What should they do first?
options: A) Ask the teaching assistants to edit each draft themselves as part of their induction
B) State who the reader is and what they already know, then try the same case again
C) Move the work to the most capable model available and re-run the same instruction
D) Rewrite every part of the arrangement at once so the next round is a clean start
correct_answers: B) State who the reader is and what they already know, then try the same case again
explanations: Pushing the rewrite onto the readers hides the design fault rather than fixing it, and the pack stays mispitched for everyone.

Correct. The fault is a missing specification, not a reasoning limit. Naming the audience and their starting knowledge addresses the actual cause, and re-running the same case shows whether it worked.
A stronger model still has no idea who the reader is; escalating tier does not supply information the instruction never contained.
Changing everything at once means that if the next draft is better, nobody will know which change was responsible.
